product.name: Shelfie
product.tagline: Your price list, open to AI shoppers.
product.audience: Sellers with a paper menu and no website, such as home bakers
valueProps: A photo of a paper price list becomes a PayPal catalog and a live shop
Any AI assistant finds the shop's agent door from its web address and orders through it
Buyers pay with PayPal, straight into the seller's own PayPal account

timeline.title: Shelfie
timeline.subtitle: Hi there! Welcome to Shelfie.
timeline.screen: Title: the Awning logo on a pomegranate band, the four-step chain motif drawing in, and "Hi there! Welcome to Shelfie."
A real handwritten paper menu (stock photo, not a particular seller), slowly zooming; the one statistic as a sourced card; then the audience line as a statement card.
timeline.narration: Picture a home baker, or a stall at the market. The menu is a sheet of paper, and there's no website. AI assistants now shop for people, but they can't order from paper. In one US survey, nearly half of food and lodging businesses had no website. Shelfie is built for them.

onScreen.text: 47% of US accommodation and food-service businesses with employees had no website.
onScreen.source: US Census Bureau, Annual Survey of Entrepreneurs (data year 2016)

onScreen.text: Shelfie is for sellers with a paper menu and no website.

timeline.screen: Laptop: Shelfie home page: the hero chain plays (paper menu, the reading, an AI order, PayPal), then the chat widget opens in the corner.
timeline.narration: Here's how it works, in three steps. Snap your price list. AI shoppers order. And you get paid on PayPal.

timeline.screen: Phone: a new seller signs up (email masked, password as dots), then adds a shop.
timeline.narration: Rosa bakes from her kitchen. She signs up with an email and a password, and adds her shop.

timeline.screen: Phone: the price list photo picked, Read my menu, Reading your menu, Check your menu.
timeline.narration: She snaps her price list. Claude, an AI model, reads every item and price in under ten seconds.

timeline.screen: Phone: the 2 for $7 question (Looks right), the PayPal email (drawn as dots), Publish, Your shop is live.
timeline.narration: It only asks about what it isn't sure of, like two for seven dollars. Rosa adds her PayPal email, so buyers pay her directly. She publishes, and every item goes into PayPal's catalog. Her shop is live.

timeline.screen: Laptop: the dashboard Share tab: Your agent door and its address.
timeline.narration: Every shop gets an agent door: an address where AI assistants read the menu and place orders. It's built on MCP, an open standard.

timeline.screen: Terminal (sped up): Claude Code with only the shop URL finds the agent door, lists products, creates the order, prints the PayPal link.
timeline.narration: Here's Claude Code, given only the shop's web address. It finds the door on its own, orders two croissants, and gets back a PayPal link.

timeline.screen: Laptop: the shop page with photos; + adds items; the cart panel with its total and Pay with PayPal.
timeline.narration: Here's her shop with photos. Tap to add, and the cart is ready for PayPal.

timeline.screen: Laptop: the shop assistant: the request with a nut allergy, the contains-nuts warning, the confirmation, the order with Approve on PayPal.
timeline.narration: Or buyers ask the shop's own assistant. This one has a nut allergy. The assistant warns that the almond croissants contain nuts, and places the order once they confirm.

timeline.screen: PayPal checkout page (Complete Purchase), then the Shelfie receipt: Paid, to Marigold Bakehouse’s own PayPal account (masked).
timeline.narration: The buyer approves on PayPal. The money goes straight into Rosa’s own PayPal account, not ours.

timeline.screen: Laptop: the dashboard toast for the paid order, the row in To prepare, the AI brief by Claude with the nut-allergy warning.
timeline.narration: Her dashboard shows the paid order. Claude reads it from PayPal and writes her a brief. It flags the nut allergy.

timeline.screen: Terminal: create_order with a price of 0.01 is refused: prices are set by the shop.
timeline.narration: And if an AI tries to set its own price, the shop refuses.

timeline.screen: Architecture card in the brand: photo → Claude reads it → PayPal catalog → agent door (MCP) → PayPal Orders, paid to the seller → Claude brief via the Agent Toolkit; each node lights as it is spoken.
timeline.narration: Under the hood, Claude reads the menu. PayPal holds the catalog and takes the payment. And the agent door lets any assistant order. For sellers like Rosa, paper is now enough.

timeline.title: Shelfie
timeline.subtitle: Your price list, open to AI shoppers.
timeline.note: End card: the Awning logo, name and line, PayPal logo, with a spoken thank-you.

positioning: Shelfie is for sellers with a paper menu and no website: one photo, and AI shoppers can order and pay.
